title: Claude Masters Class
description: A full Claude apprenticeship: long-context reasoning, structured prompting, research synthesis, writing systems, analysis workflows, and shipping reliable knowledge work end to end.

lessons.title: Claude Strengths and Working Modes

introduction.text: Claude excels at careful reasoning, long documents, rewriting with voice control, and turning messy notes into structured plans. Treat it as a senior analyst who still needs your judgment on facts, taste, and risk. Choose modes deliberately: brainstorm, critique, draft, or extract. This apprenticeship builds end-to-end habits for research, writing, and decision support—not one-off chat tricks.

lessons.title: Structured Prompting and Output Contracts

introduction.text: High-yield Claude prompts declare role, goal, inputs, constraints, and an output contract (sections, bullets, JSON-like fields, or tables). Ask Claude to list assumptions before answering when stakes are high. Prefer checkable formats over free prose when the result feeds another step.

questions.question: An output contract tells Claude:
options: Exactly how to shape the answer
questions.correctAnswer: Exactly how to shape the answer

questions.question: Listing assumptions helps you:
options: Surface gaps before acting on advice
questions.correctAnswer: Surface gaps before acting on advice

questions.question: Checkable formats beat free prose when:
options: Another human or tool must reuse the result
questions.correctAnswer: Another human or tool must reuse the result

lessons.title: Long-Context Research and Synthesis

introduction.text: Paste or attach source packs with clear labels. Ask Claude to separate facts, inferences, and open questions. Demand quote anchors and contradiction flags. Synthesis is not summary theater—it should produce decisions, options, or a brief you can defend.

questions.question: Contradiction flags matter because:
options: Conflicts change what you can claim
questions.correctAnswer: Conflicts change what you can claim

lessons.title: Analysis Workflows and Decision Memos

introduction.text: Use Claude to pressure-test options: criteria, tradeoffs, second-order effects, and kill criteria. Demand a decision memo format stakeholders can skim. Separate recommendation from confidence and from what would change your mind.

lessons.title: Projects, Artifacts, and Team Reuse

introduction.text: Turn winning Claude chats into team artifacts: prompt libraries, checklists, memo templates, and review rubrics. Version them. Teach teammates when Claude is leverage vs when human research is required. Masters craft is institutional, not personal folklore.

questions.correctAnswer: Tools and norms change over time

questions.question: Human research is required when:
options: Stakes and novelty are high or sources are thin
questions.correctAnswer: Stakes and novelty are high or sources are thin
